mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals an easing monetary policy that reduces equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods with three consecutive monthly FEDFUNDS declines over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.2 percentage points from the prior month signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE increases by >0.2pp from prior month over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a contraction in consumer demand that triggers negative earnings outlooks, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where both HOUST and RSAFS decline from prior month over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During sustained manufacturing supply chain disruptions (INDPRO below 105 for two consecutive months), S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to inflationary pressures and reduced corporate margins.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where INDPRO < 105 for two consecutive months over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in retail sales (RSAFS) consistently indicates strengthening consumer spending that boosts corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods with three consecutive monthly RSAFS increases over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months, it signals restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and dampens equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and declines in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicate a weakening labor market that reduces consumer confidence and spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where UNRATE increases and PAYEMS decreases from prior month over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic regimes characterized by high labor market tightness (UNRATE below 4.5% and PAYEMS growth above 0.5% monthly), S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to inflationary pressures and premature monetary tightening.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where UNRATE < 4.5% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly over a 5-year rolling window.
